requested_visible_change: Make the articles hub, scenario, preparation guide and budget article visibly one corporate wedding-editorial system instead of four page-specific Hero layouts.
expected_visible_delta: At the same viewport, every route has the same service-line anchor, portrait focal point, H1/lead scale and author-row anchor; the budget route adds calculator buttons without changing the composition.

served_candidate.source_ref: fresh local Astro preview from the current working tree

target.surface: shared .tg-article-hero across four public wedding routes
target.action: direct navigation to each route in a freshly opened local browser tab

must_remain_unchanged: Article copy, URLs and SEO metadata
Telegram/MAX calculator destinations and source codes
Black-and-white portrait and dark corporate treatment

observations.viewport_source: Playwright exact resize in the permanent articles-hub probe
observations.before_signature: The hub could receive its own compact Hero measure and drift from the editorial articles.
observations.after_signature: The hub uses the same short-desktop grid as every wedding route: kicker top=40px, short-scale H1/lead and byline bottom gap=40px.
observations.observed_visible_result: The catalogue first screen is a complete shared Hero rather than a separate landing composition, with the author row fully visible.

observations.viewport_source: Playwright exact resize in the strict four-route comparison gate
observations.before_signature: The four routes could select different title, CTA and focal rules at this wide-short desktop size.
observations.after_signature: All four routes use the global short-height mode, a common 660px H1 measure, portrait background-position=74% 0% and equal cross-route anchors and type metrics.
observations.observed_visible_result: No route clips the portrait head or pushes the author row outside the first desktop frame.

observations.viewport_source: Playwright exact resize in the strict route-comparison gate
observations.before_signature: Production had compact/CTA Hero branches and an aspect-ratio focal override; the owner observed mismatched service positions, type scale and clipped hair across the four routes.
observations.after_signature: All four routes render one desktop 660px H1 measure and H1/lead scale, kicker top=72px, byline bottom gap=76px and portrait background-position=74% 0%; the gate compares these values across routes.
observations.observed_visible_result: The shared portrait keeps the whole head inside frame and the author/service hierarchy matches across the catalogue, scenario, preparation and budget routes.

observations.viewport_source: Playwright exact resize in the permanent budget first-screen gate
observations.before_signature: The budget Hero either exceeded the initial viewport or reduced only its own spacing through a CTA-specific mode.
observations.after_signature: The global very-short mode renders the budget title, lead, both 42px controls and author row in the initial viewport; reduced shared byline internal padding preserves air above the author row. Hero bottom=583px including its border, portrait background-position=74% 0%.
observations.observed_visible_result: The full budget entry stays readable and complete without a page-specific Hero variant; the author row has visible air below the buttons.

observations.viewport_source: Playwright exact resize in the responsive matrix
observations.before_signature: Mobile inherited differing page-level Hero branches and a lower portrait focal point.
observations.after_signature: All four routes use the same mobile type role, 20px service-to-title gap and portrait background-position=72% 0% with no horizontal overflow.
observations.observed_visible_result: The mobile Hero remains readable, the portrait head stays visible and the budget's messenger controls remain usable.

comparison_review.owner_approval_reference: Owner-supplied /scenario/ comparison screenshot as the intended editorial hierarchy
